meta.description: Academic reference multi-source verification: field-by-field comparison (author, title, year, volume, issue, pages), marks volume-year/DOI-year conflicts, author order anomalies, page deviations. Batch processing for entire paper reference lists or single-item verification. Supports Zotero sync correction. Five-step workflow (parse input → multi-source parallel query → field-level comparison → confidence assessment → output report). Severity grading (Critical/Warning/Info).

scientific_integrity.detail: Multi-source cross-verification (Crossref, IEEE Xplore, CNKI, WebSearch, Zotero) prevents reliance on single source. Field-level comparison detects author errors, DOI misattribution, page deviations. Step 2.0 DOI resolvability check (404 vs 200 + metadata comparison) catches common errors early.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for reference verification. Severity grading (Critical/Warning/Info) prioritizes fixes correctly. Does not auto-correct without user review. Unverifiable references marked (not fabricated). Early Access metadata drift handling (use CrossRef current values).

methodological_ground.detail: Multi-source parallel query strategy sound (DOI → Crossref, failure → title+author web search). Field-level comparison comprehensive (author, title, year, volume, issue, pages, DOI, journal). Confidence assessment (Verified/Check suggested/Needs fix/Unverifiable) logical.

code_usability.detail: Five-step workflow clear. Batch strategy (20+ refs → 10-15 per parallel subagent). Output formats (Markdown report, BibTeX patch, Zotero update instructions). Environment dependencies documented (pyzotero, zotero-cli, kimi-datasource, webbridge).

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive verification: field-level comparison (author, title, year, vol, issue, pages, DOI, journal), multi-source query (Crossref, IEEE, CNKI, WebSearch, Zotero), three input formats (full paper, single ref, BibTeX), severity grading (Critical/Warning/Info), batch processing with parallel subagents. Minor: no explicit journal abbreviation normalization (IET vs IEE as Warning only).

reliability.note: Strong quality checks: Step 2.0 DOI resolvability (404 vs 200 + metadata) catches common errors, multi-source cross-verification prevents single-source bias, field-level comparison comprehensive, Early Access metadata drift handling (CrossRef current values). Minor: no validation that parallel subagents don't duplicate queries (efficiency concern).

performance_context.note: Efficient batch strategy: 20+ refs → 10-15 per parallel subagent (3 subagents for 35 refs, one roundtrip vs sequential magnitude slower). DOI-first cheapest check (Step 2.0) before expensive web searches. Progressive degradation (DOI → title+author search).

agent_usability.note: Clear five-step workflow. Severity grading explicit (Critical 7 cases, Warning 7 cases, Info 3 cases). Multi-source strategy documented. Batch threshold clear (20+ refs). Minor: common-patterns.md on-demand loading mentioned but loading conditions not fully specified. Zotero write path complexity (2026 limitations) requires external knowledge.

human_usability.note: Good output formats: Markdown summary report with tables, BibTeX patch, Zotero update instructions. Bilingual documentation (Chinese). Confidence levels intuitive (✅⚠️❌❓). Typical cases documented. Minor: Zotero write path complexity (localhost:23119 read-only, pyzotero Web mode, connector/saveItems limitations, sqlite as last resort) may confuse non-technical users.

security.note: Excellent boundaries: does not auto-correct without user review, unverifiable refs marked (not fabricated), multi-source verification prevents malicious single-source manipulation. Zotero sqlite edit only when Zotero closed (prevents corruption). No credential exposure in examples.

maintainability.note: Good modular design: five-step workflow, severity grading table, multi-source strategy, known limitations table. Environment dependencies clearly listed with fallback paths. Manifest.yaml mentioned for routing. Extension points for new sources clear.

agent_specific.note: Strong parallel batch strategy: 10-15 refs per subagent, 3 subagents for 35 refs. Multi-source query efficient. Minor: no explicit deduplication of queries across parallel subagents. No token budget estimation for very large reference lists (200+ refs). Zotero integration complex (multiple write paths) may require external tool skill.

Strong batch processing: parallel subagents (10-15 refs each), 35 refs in one roundtrip with 3 subagents vs sequential magnitude slower
Comprehensive field-level comparison: author (name, order, missing), title, year, volume, issue, pages, DOI, journal with severity grading (Critical/Warning/Info)

recommendations.title: Add query deduplication across parallel subagents
recommendations.problem: Batch strategy dispatches 3 parallel subagents for 35 refs (12+12+11) but no explicit deduplication if same DOI/title appears in multiple subagent chunks. Could result in duplicate queries to Crossref/IEEE/CNKI.
recommendations.root_cause: Parallel dispatch optimizes for speed but doesn't coordinate queries across subagents.
recommendations.fix: Add query coordination: (1) collect all DOIs/titles before dispatch, (2) deduplicate at dispatch time (assign unique refs only), (3) OR add shared query cache (first subagent to query caches result, others reuse). Document in batch strategy section. Include cache invalidation for user-corrected refs.

recommendations.title: Add explicit article number pattern validation
recommendations.problem: Article number letter misinterpretation (文章号字母误判) documented with T/7 example but no explicit check for all common confusions (T/7, l/1, O/0, I/1, S/5, Z/2). Single case detected but comprehensive pattern matching not enforced.
recommendations.root_cause: Letter-digit confusion detection likely manual comparison, not pattern-based.
recommendations.fix: Add article number validation: (1) pattern library for common confusions {T:7, l:1, I:1, O:0, S:5, Z:2}, (2) if article number differs, check if substitution by confusion pattern matches, (3) flag as Critical with specific confusion identified (e.g., 'T→7 in 101880T'). Include reverse check (1018807 → 10188O7 possible?).

recommendations.title: Add field-level diff highlighting in BibTeX patch
recommendations.problem: BibTeX patch output provides corrected entries but doesn't explicitly highlight which fields changed (author, volume, pages). User must manually compare original vs patch to see differences.
recommendations.root_cause: Patch format documented but diff mechanism not specified.
recommendations.fix: Add to BibTeX patch output: (1) comment block above each corrected entry listing changed fields (% CHANGED: author (order), pages (10437→1)), (2) inline field comments (author = {Corrected Name}, % was: {Wrong Name}), (3) optional unified diff format (.patch file) for programmers. Document in Step 5 output formats.
